message.content:
There isn’t a single definitive “best” jazz singer—different voices and styles resonate with different listeners—but a few names consistently appear at the top of lists and are widely regarded as defining figures in the genre:

| Singer | Why they’re celebrated |
|--------|------------------------|
| **Ella Fitzgerald** | Known as the “First Lady of Song,” her impeccable pitch, scat‑sing mastery, and effortless phrasing set a gold standard for vocal jazz. |
| **Billie Holiday** | Her deeply emotive delivery and unique phrasing turned standards into personal statements; she’s often cited as the most influential jazz vocalist of all time. |
| **Louis Armstrong** (vocalist) | Though primarily a trumpeter, his gravelly, charismatic singing style helped bring jazz to a mainstream audience. |
| **Sarah Vaughan** | A modern icon whose blend of jazz, pop, and soul has earned her critical acclaim and a Grammy for “At Last.” |
| **Cassandra Wilson** | A contemporary voice who blends traditional jazz with modern sensibilities, earning her a reputation as one of the leading jazz singers of her generation. |

If you’re looking for a definitive “best,” many would point to **Ella Fitzgerald** for her technical brilliance and timeless influence, but the “best” can vary depending on whether you value vocal technique, emotional depth, or innovation.
